# VIctory

Runs Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series X|S) natively on Windows, from files
the user supplies.

The title's x86-64 code runs unchanged inside our process; VIctory supplies
the platform underneath it and converts the title's data, ahead of time where
it can (shaders and pipelines too, see Getting started) and on first use
otherwise. See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Status (2026-11-25)

**Not playable yet, because of the framerate: about 1 frame per second in the
world.** Nothing else keeps the game from working: the title boots, runs its
menus at its own 30 fps, loads the world, plays the intro cutscene and
reaches the **prologue**, the mission after it, with the graphics fully
displayed. 

| Stage | State |
|-------|-------|
| Boot, first-boot screens (accessibility, language, settings, legal) | works, 30 fps |
| Intro video with sound | works |
| Start screen, profile and saves | works |
| Loading into the world (about a minute) | works |
| The intro cutscene | plays at about 1 fps (0.9-1.0 s a frame, warm cache, quiet machine): textured and lit characters with whole hair, buildings, sky, depth of field, the title card, credits and interface. Missing: ray-traced shadows and indirect light, the local-light shadow mask. Seen in some shots: a pink band over nearer bodies, a stand-in head on a secondary character for a few frames |
| The prologue | reached; the graphics are fully displayed, at about 1 fps |

In the intro cutscene at 1 fps the opening credits land over other shots than
on a console: they follow the frame count, the shots follow the clock.

Tested on one machine: Windows 11, AMD RX 6700 XT (12 GB).

> **Warning.** Entering the world on a real GPU hung it in earlier builds,
> and Windows then reset the display driver (every monitor goes black for a
> moment). The latest runs, several minutes each in the world, did not, but
> it is not ruled out; a run can also end on a GPU fault (`crashes.log`). A
> diagnostics build with `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1` renders on the software
> adapter instead (too slow to reach the world in minutes).

What each part does today and what it still needs:

| Subsystem | Today | Needs |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Loader | Runs the title's executable and its DLLs in our process; crash reports name the faulting code and are kept in `crashes.log` | – |
| Runtime services | One signed-in offline user, licences, packages, saves that survive a kill at any step, text entry dialog | Speech is silent; the dialog and relaunch are untested live |
| Network | Offline by design: the title cannot reach the network | – |
| Files and streaming | Archives and streamed data read, zlib and BCPack decoded in parallel | Loading is limited by writes into title memory |
| Input | XInput pads, keyboard, keyboard stand-in pad | Trigger rumble |
| Audio | Menu, video and loading sound; XMA voices and Opus streams decode | Reverb is silent; Opus results unverified against the title |
| GPU: menus | Draws, compute and presentation on host D3D12; only changed title memory is copied | Frame pacing drifts on one screen in release builds |
| GPU: world | The scene is drawn and presented: mesh pipelines, indirect execution, views the shaders pick from the heap themselves, title memory read by address, depth written from compute, lists that wait for values other queues write, textures made when a shader first reads them, pipelines pre-built or made by worker threads and kept on disk, depth bounds on supporting adapters (synthetic tests) | The title's ray-tracing structures are never built (no ray-traced shadows or indirect light in the intro cutscene); about 1 s a frame; draws of untranslated shaders are dropped; real queries, HDR and scaling are missing |
| Shaders | Console GPU code recompiled to DXIL, ahead of time (`translate --cache`) or at first use, cached on disk. Menus: all. World: all but under 300 of 24,387 programs | Merged geometry stages (195 programs) and under 100 others; fused multiply-adds follow the host GPU; some compute programs need a GPU with 64-lane waves |
| Textures | Console tiled layouts and detiling for the modes the title uses | Render-target metadata planes |
| Series S mode | Menus, loading and the world run with the PC upscaler (`VICTORY_FIDELITYFX_DIR`, about 1 s a frame) | The title's own upscaler DLLs: six of their passes are untranslated, so their picture is wrong |

content.readme:

# XCL – Xbox Series X|S → Windows compatibility layer XCL is a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) games you own on a Windows PC - in the spirit of Wine/Proton. There is no CPU emulation: the game's x64 code runs natively, and XCL provides its own, independently written implementations of the console system libraries the PC does not have (`kernelx.dll`, XGameRuntime, `d3d12_xs.dll`, …). The console's GPU code (RDNA2 machine code) is recompiled into PC shaders (HLSL → DXIL). > [!IMPORTANT] > XCL works only on unpacked game files you already own. It does not download, decrypt or unpack game packages (XVC / MSIXVC) and contains nothing for circumventing DRM. The repository holds no code, headers or binaries from the console SDK, no keys and no game data; the Windows components XCL relies on (XGameRuntime, XAudio2, D3D12, DXC) come from your own system or the public Windows SDK and are not distributed with XCL.

content.readme:
Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow.

Rewriting a whole app in Rust costs months, minute-long compiles and gigabytes of `target/`. Most of the runtime sits in a few functions anyway. **fast-anything** finds those functions, has your coding agent port *only them* to Rust, proves the port gives the same results on real recorded calls, and swaps it in. One command, fully reversible.

## Install ```sh npm i -g @el4cteo/fast-anything # or: cargo install fast-anything ``` Ports are compiled with your Rust toolchain ([rustup](https://rustup.rs)). ## Use ```sh fast-anything go --agent claude -- python app.py # or: -- node app.ts / bun app.ts / deno run -A app.ts / ruby app.rb / java App.java / mvn exec:java / gradle run / go run . / php app.php / clang -O2 main.c / Rscript app.R ``` Or step by step: | command | what it does | |---|---| | `scan -- ` | profiles the app, ranks functions by time × how portable they are | | `port [id]` | records up to 500 real calls, creates a one-function Rust crate + `TASK.md` | | `verify` | release-builds the port and replays every recorded call | | `enable` / `disable` | swaps the Rust in or out (one marked block, removed byte for byte) | | `bench` | times the whole app in rotated rounds of original, original again (an A/A control for noise) and Rust, plus one warm-up per side (`--runs 5` = 11 original runs, 6 Rust runs); wall and CPU time | | `report` | markdown + SVG card for your PR | | `doctor` | checks Rust, your runtimes and your agents | `--agent` takes `claude`, `codex`, or any command that reads a prompt on stdin. Without it, hand `TASK.md` to whatever you use. ## Proof, not vibes

That port looked right but compared bytes instead of characters. 148 of 500 real calls caught it. On top of the recorded calls, fast-anything derives extra cases and lets the original answer them: edge cases (NaN, ±infinity, -0.0, zero and ±1, non-ASCII text, empty and up to 16× bigger inputs) and shrunk inputs (tiny and random slices). Nothing is enabled until every case matches: same values (floats within 1e-9 of their size or of the largest value in the same list, -0.0 not 0.0), errors where the original errors. A port that is right but slower per call than the original (calling into Rust costs more than the work saved) isn't enabled either, nor is one whose original takes about as long as a clock read (where each call is timed on its own: C, C++, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, C#), since the per-call times can't show a saving there. `FAST_ANYTHING_DISABLE=1` runs the original any time. Every 5th recorded call (from 5 calls up) is held out of the crate folder the agent works in: verify replays it too but reports a mismatch there without the values, so a port that special-cases the calls it was shown still fails. verify deletes its working copy of those calls when it's done. It's a guard against a port fitted to the calls it was shown, not a sandbox: an agent that goes looking can still read them in `.fast/holdout`. ## Results Real runs on an i5-10500, Windows 11 (C and C++: a 4-core GitHub Actions Linux runner). Reproduce them from [`examples/`](examples). | app

# VIctory on an RX 7900 XTX

A fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a compatibility layer
that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from files the user supplies.

## The goal

**A stable 30 fps or more without ray tracing, then as high a frame rate and as
low frame times as the PC allows**, on an AMD RX 7900 XTX first and on PCs with
32 GB (later 16 GB) of RAM.

The way there is **porting, not emulating**: patching the title's renderer so it
behaves the way a PC renderer does, rather than having the layer watch and copy
the console's shared memory every frame. Shaders are translated ahead of time
into a versioned store that is kept between builds. Ray tracing stays optional
and off by default. The picture comes after the frame rate: texture pop-in and
lighting that is too bright or too dark when walking indoors are next in line.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's developer
or publisher.

## Where it stands (2026-11-26)

The measurements below come from one Windows 11 PC with an Intel i9-12900K,
64 GB of system RAM and a Radeon RX 7900 XTX (24 GB of dedicated video memory).
Ray tracing was off for these runs.

| | |
|---|---|
| City street, Series S profile, renderer patches 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 on | about 45 ms a frame (about 22 fps, 44.9 ms in run merge-5) |
| Same, patches 1, 2, 5 and 6 | 45.6 ms, p95 47 ms |
| Same, patches 1, 2 and 5 | 47.3 ms (about 21 fps), p95 49 ms |
| Series X profile, patches 1+2 | about 53 ms (about 19 fps) |
| Same scene before the patches | 57-75 ms (13-17 fps) |
| Shaders the title uses that translate | all of them (25,790 of 25,985; the rest are unused geometry shaders) |
| Memory | about 30 GB of private memory, 10.5 GB of VRAM: **64 GB of RAM recommended** for now |

It started at 280 ms a frame in the same scenes three days earlier. What sets
the frame now is the one thread that submits the title's work to the card
(about 40 ms); the card itself needs about 36 ms and now waits about 7 ms a frame with nothing queued.

### Reports from other GPUs

| GPU and build | What the contributor observed |
|---|---|
| Radeon RX 9060 XT (16 GB), `cd8dfc0` with local changes | In the same Series X interior at 1080p, the game averaged 19.8 fps with ray tracing off and 15.6 fps with it on. Indirect lighting showed white patches and dark smears. [Run settings and results](https://github.com/Belobug/VIctory-Belobug-AMD/issues/313) |
| GeForce RTX 3090 (24 GB), `a-publier@cd8dfc0` | The prison rendered. Two warm Series S runs averaged 545 and 532 ms per frame. The contributor reported 10.0 and 10.2 GB of VRAM in those runs. [Run settings and results](https://github.com/Belobug/VIctory-Belobug-AMD/issues/333) |
| Intel Arc B580 (12 GB), revision unreported | Startup and initial menu navigation worked. Further menu interaction slowed to about 0.7 fps before D3D12 device removal. [Crash report](https://github.com/Belobug/VIctory-Belobug-AMD/issues/98) |

The 10.5 GB of VRAM in the RX 7900 XTX table is the usage reported for that run.
Memory use and frame time depend on the scene and settings. The [ray-tracing notes](docs/fork-ray-tracing.md)
describe which lighting paths run and the remaining rendering issues.

### Renderer patches (off by default while they are tested)

| Switch | What it does |
|---|---|
| `VICTORY_PORT_CONSTANTS=1` | The title's 174 MB constants heap is read by the card where the title writes it: no uploads, no fills |
| `VICTORY_PORT_DESCRIPTORS=1` | The title's descriptor-table stores are patched (byte-checked) to report the slots they write, instead of a scan of ~600,000 slots a frame |
| `VICTORY_PORT_CBV=1` | Translated shaders read constant buffers in place as raw bytes (~22,000 fills a frame to none; -4.7 ms) |
| `VICTORY_PORT_GUARD=1` | The write guards' lock is shared by faults and refreshes, with a claim per 64 KiB block; the submission's planning runs beside it (title threads' waits 29 ms to ~2 ms a frame; -2 ms) |
| `VICTORY_PORT_JOURNAL=1` | The heaps' records are asked for at the title's submit, and the journal's notes are split into 64 parts with locks of their own (the submit thread's waits ~5 ms + 1 ms to ~0.3 ms; -1 to -3 ms) |

### Other switches

| Switch | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--console series-s` | The Series S profile: 1080p output, about 5 ms faster, a softer picture |
| `VICTORY_OUTPUT=1920x1080` | The title renders to that output size itself (Series X profile; about 16 ms less card time) |
| `VICTORY_FRAME_INTERVAL_MS=16.667` | Lets the title go above 30 fps (menus and videos reach 60; the game's clock stays right) |
| `VICTORY_AMBIENT_SETTLE` | How fast light settles after walking indoors (on by default, `250,3`; `0` turns it off) |
| `VICTORY_TEXTURE_STORE=1` | Converted textures kept between runs (about 8 ms a frame for now: off) |
| `VICTORY_KBM_GTA=1` | Optional GTA V PC-style keyboard and mouse mapping

content.readme:
# CHIMERA

A physical-modeling voice synthesizer in the browser. Every sound comes from a simulated
airway (lungs, vocal folds or syrinx, a branched vocal tract, lips, nose), not from samples.
The engine is Rust, compiled to WebAssembly for an AudioWorklet; the same code runs natively
for tests and the `chimera` CLI.

## Vision & scope

1. **One instrument**: a physically modeled voice (lungs, vocal folds, throat, mouth). No
   samples, no neural audio.
2. **The web app is the primary surface**: anyone should be able to make songs in it without
   an LLM's help. Mobile is the likely next surface. The plugin (CLAP/VST3/AU) still ships, but
   it's secondary.
3. **As realistic as we can make it**: the main push is to see how close the simulation gets to
   a real voice. The robotic, Vocaloid-like sound people like today stays playable as a preset
   ([#93](https://github.com/jamesondh/chimera-vocal-synth/issues/93)).
4. **Languages enter through one shared front-end design**, not one-off hacks. Each needs a
   native speaker's check and must leave English unchanged.
5. **The design language (the vector display) is settled**; the look within it can still evolve.
6. **Nothing copyrighted in git**; MIT; a deterministic, real-time-safe engine.
7. **The 3D head can be worn by a body** ([docs/rig.md](docs/rig.md)), for the videos people
   make with the voice, posed by joint angles or moved by other tools' motion (Mixamo, BVH,
   glTF): a small library, not animation software (no timeline, no renderer).
8. **Not now**: a DAW or sequencer, a light theme, multi-voice dialogue, translating the
   interface (the voice speaks and sings many languages; the labels stay in English).

## What it does

- **Play**: drag the tongue, lips and jaw in a live cutaway of the head; vowel pad, encoders,
  computer keyboard and Web MIDI.
- **Speak**: English text (CMUdict with a letter-to-sound fallback), Turkish text (EN/TR) or
  IPA, turned into gestures and prosody, with the gestural score and a consonant chart on screen.
  In IPA mode a notice under the box lists the symbols and marks the voice doesn't say
  (`chimera render speech` prints the same as warnings).
- **Sing**: type words and the **Sing** button sings them to a tune picked by its mood, each line
  fitted to a phrase of it (Tempo and Key on the Voice screen); **Record video** sings it again into a
  9:16 clip to share. The keys sing the same words a syllable at a time, legato or not, onto a
  pitch roll; consonants land before the beat. Lyrics can be English, Turkish (chosen with EN/TR:
  Latin script can't tell them apart), Korean (Hangul: one block per note, with Korean sound
  rules), Japanese (kana, one mora per note) or Russian; each language is a front end
  ([docs/language-front-ends.md](docs/language-front-ends.md)).
- **Beatbox**: pads and a step sequencer, every drum an articulatory gesture.
- **Bestiary**: songbird (two-voice syrinx), seal, alligator and elephant.
- **Duet** (`?show=<id>`): two 3D heads replay a pre-rendered song.

Male, female and child bodies blend continuously. Everything on screen animates from live
engine state: pressure in the airway, airflow, the vocal folds, spectra and formants.

## Run it

Needs Rust with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, and Bun.

```sh
bun install
bun run dev        # builds the wasm, then Vite on 127.0.0.1:5317
bun run test       # wasm build, cargo test --workspace, bun test tests
```

The AudioWorklet needs a secure context, so open it on localhost or over HTTPS (for example
`tailscale serve`). Vercel builds it with `vercel.json`.

## As a plugin

Early: a CLAP, VST3 and AU instrument for macOS, and CLAP and VST3 for Windows, with the same UI in
a webview, in a window you can resize. On Linux (CLAP and VST3) the same UI opens in your web browser.
MIDI notes sing the lyrics, one syllable per note (Sing); play the posture you've set (Play); say
the next line of text (Speak); or play mouth drums and hum, with a beat that follows the host's tempo
(Beatbox). Everything saves with the project, and the voice parameters can be automated.

On a Mac (signed and notarised) or on Linux (x86_64), the release installs with one command (or
download it from [chimera.audio/plugin](https://chimera.audio/plugin/)):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://chimera.audio/install.sh | sh
```

To build it yourself, with Xcode's command line tools as well as the above:

```sh
crates/chimera-plugin/macos/build.sh --install
```

Or, with GitHub's `gh` logged in, install CI's newest build without building anything:

```sh
crates/chimera-plugin/macos/update.sh
```

To build it on Linux: `crates/chimera-plugin/linux/build.sh --install`. On Windows, in Git Bash with
Rust's MSVC toolchain: `crates/chimera-plugin/windows/build.sh --install`. The Windows build isn't
released yet. See [docs/plugin.md](docs/plugin.md), "Releases".

Offline renders and measurement:

```sh
cargo run --release -p chimera-cli -- render speech|text|song|notes|beatbox|creature|v

# VIctory fork (work in progress)

A work-in-progress fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a
compatibility layer that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from
files the user supplies. This fork follows upstream
`main` and adds fixes aimed at one goal: getting the game's world to render
correctly and playably on one particular PC.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's
developer or publisher.

## Credits

- **[VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory)** by Marvisak and its
  contributors is the base of everything here: the loader, the runtime
  services, the Direct3D 12 back end and the shader recompiler. Licensed
  GPL-3.0-or-later; so is this fork. Upstream's history is kept intact below
  the single commit that carries this fork's changes.
- **[XCL](https://github.com/ivall/xcl)** by ivall and its contributors
  (GPL-2.0-only) was used as a reference for how the same title behaves under
  another layer. Fixes inspired by it were written anew in VIctory's code.
- The guard over every view of a memory page is code by **myokex**
  ([victory-amd](https://github.com/myokex/victory-amd), commit `c6dc4d8`), which
  adapts pull request #115 here by Spexivus, its correction by joroyt and a part of
  VIctory #1122 by tightfall. The read-beside fix for kernel reads into title
  memory is by **Joshua Odom** (commit `10ea38e` of the same fork family). Both
  are carried here unchanged apart from one merge conflict.
- This fork's changes were developed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

## Status of this fork (2026-11-27, 06:30 UTC)

**Playable, slowly: about 11 world frames per second at the first boat mission at 1,500 to 3,300
draws (usual frame 88 ms), 8.5 at 3,300 and more (115 to 120 ms); the console runs 30. The card is no
longer the limit (53 to 66 ms a frame, the submitting thread waits for it about 0 ms); the thread that
prepares submissions is (65 to 87 ms a frame at work). The
open water now shows waves and the sun's path with no black patches. The tester has played from the opening through the prologue and past
the first boat mission. The graphics card is still lost now and then 30 to 50 minutes into a session,
before the title's next save point; cause not known yet. **New: with the ray-tracing structure builder on
(the default) the title's ray-traced shadows and light now show once a scene has streamed in (tester,
2026-11-27), but the frame rate falls to about 0.2 to 3 a second while it runs; set
`VICTORY_BVH_BUILDER=0` to play at the speeds above.**
Tested on one machine: Windows 11, Intel i7-14700KF, NVIDIA RTX 4070 12 GB,
32 GB RAM. The Series X profile is used throughout.

| Stage | State in this fork |
|-------|--------------------|
| Boot, menus, start screen | works, 30 fps (as upstream) |
| Opening cutscene | plays from start to finish, in order, lit: title cards, credits cards, night and dusk shots |
| Saves | the game autosaves a checkpoint and loads it again; test runs continue from the last checkpoint |
| The prologue and the first missions | play: characters, textures, sky, sunlit exteriors, vehicles and boats; HUD, pause menu and pad input work. Played past the first boat mission (2026-11-25) |
| Water | **2026-11-27: no black or grey patches on open water** once the two 64-lane water programs (5dc3b25986622949, 6f225b641c5b0708) are no longer forced into the wave-wide form (leave them out of `VICTORY_WAVE_WIDE_ONLY`). Before: right since `VICTORY_TEXTURE_BACK=1` (pull request #999): boats float, the surface is lit (blue, waves, the sun's path). Without it boats sink and the mission fails |
| Light in shadow | **2026-11-27: ray-traced shadows and light show with the builder on, after a scene has streamed in (minutes at the low frame rate; the first minutes still show stand-in models and black faces).** Without the builder (`VICTORY_BVH_BUILDER=0`) anything the sun does not hit directly is black |
| Frame rate in the world | **2026-11-26 evening: usual world frame 131 ms at 3,300 to 4,100 draws with the card at 80 ms a frame (card hashing a group of 64 threads a piece, now the default; 149 ms and 108 ms of card without it, run 349).** Earlier: 8.2 to 8.6 world frames a second at the first boat mission at 3,000 to 5,000 draws, 9.5 over a whole standing run** (runs 311, 312, 315, 316: frames counted only where every frame is a world frame, not fades or loading screens), with the texture pass on its own thread (`VICTORY_HEAP_WORKER=1`; 6.2 to 6.7 without it). 10 to 14 fps at 500 to 1,500 draws. The thread that prepares submissions is the limit (about 70 ms of a usual frame); the card is at work about 9 ms. It started at 3 to 6 seconds a frame. Measured with the switch set in `diagnostics/README.md`; the defaults are slower |
| Stability | **the card is lost after 30 to 50 minutes of play**: Windows reports the device removed (0x887A0005)

**微信、QQ 未读提醒**：收起时亮起图标和红点，展开后在面板旁查看，点击切换到对应窗口。 - **微信多开分开看**：不同账号分别显示，点击对应账号的未读图标即可切换。 - **按需显示通知正文**：默认隐藏正文；开启预览后仍遮罩识别出的验证码。 - **微信提醒不读取聊天正文**：根据任务栏闪动提示新消息。微信缩在托盘时，可选开启「托盘一键唤起微信」。 - **企业微信、飞书和钉钉**：在消息提醒设置里分别开启，并确认对应客户端允许任务栏闪动。新消息会在岛上提醒，点一下即可打开对应窗口。 在 **设置 → 消息提醒** 开启「微信」。QQ 可从「QQ 与其他应用 → 连接…」选择「只连接 QQ」，并在 QQ 中启用 Windows 系统通知。 ## 换个皮肤，也换个位置 ![五款皮肤：经典黑、奶油、毛玻璃浅色、毛玻璃深色、悬浮云；刘海和胶囊两种形态](docs/images/readme/appearance.webp) **五款皮肤 × 两种形态，自由搭配。** 经典黑、奶油、毛玻璃·浅、毛玻璃·深和「悬浮云」，都能搭配刘海或胶囊。毛玻璃透出身后的桌面；悬浮云随专辑封面换色，光晕跟着鼠标移动。 ![顶部、左侧和右侧停靠，以及侧边收起与展开状态](docs/images/readme/docking.webp) - **四边停靠**：顶部和底部横向排列，底部向上展开，会跟随自动隐藏的任务栏。左右侧边收起为竖向胶囊，鼠标靠近后从屏幕边缘展开。 - **大小与位置可调**：岛体大小支持 80%–140%，上下停靠可左右移动，侧边可上下调整。展开后按住日期时间，可以切换停靠边或把小岛拖到另一块屏幕。 - **OLED 像素偏移**（默认关闭）：收起静止时沿停靠边缓慢移动几个像素，帮助减轻 OLED 静态显示留下的痕迹。 - **多屏与自动避让**：跟随主屏或固定到指定显示器。前台浏览器或自定义应用的窗口遮住岛时，岛会收成贴边细线。切到插件浮窗时，如果名单里的宿主窗口仍遮住岛，岛会继续避让。 - **按习惯显示**：支持极简模式、12／24 小时制，以及功能页面开关与拖动排序。 在 **设置 → 外观／位置** 里分别调整皮肤、形态和停靠。岛上单行歌词支持顶部和底部停靠。 在 **设置 → 通用** 开启「在截图和录屏中隐藏岛仔」后，桌面照常显示小岛，兼容的截图和录屏工具会略过它。该选项需要 Windows 10 2004 或更新版本。 ## 插件集市 官方和社区一起为小岛扩展功能。插件可以更换外观材质、增加功能页，也可以扩展页面切换和无线设备兼容。 ![岛仔插件集市，展示液态玻璃、我的日子和现货金价](docs/images/readme/plugin-market.webp) 集市里有**液态玻璃、我的日子、现货金价、实时工资、便签本、世界时钟、页面快捷切换和无线设备兼容包**等插件。 [浏览岛仔插件仓](https://github.com/Renly1994/xiaotang-daozai-plugins) ## 听歌时，歌词就在抬眼处 ![音乐播放控制、展开歌词与收起状态下的岛上单行歌词](docs/images/readme/music.webp) 播放、暂停、切歌、调节音量和拖动进度，都能在岛上操作。展开看歌词，也可以收起后只留一行歌词，让桌面继续做自己的事。 - 通过 Windows 媒体会话读取播放信息，并针对网易云音乐、QQ 音乐、酷狗、汽水音乐和波点音乐补充兼容。 - 网易云优先按歌曲 ID 找词，改善译名、合唱署名和 Live／Remix 等不同版本的匹配。 - 切歌、暂停和拖动进度时更快同步到岛上，改善了网易云和酷狗部分版本的进度适配。 播放器需提供可用的媒体信息；歌词取决于歌曲元数据与歌词来源，个别歌曲或播放器版本可能无法显示。 ## 日程、待办和专注，放在一起 ![日历与会议安排、每周重复待办、番茄专注与饮水提醒](docs/images/readme/daily.webp) | 想做的事 | 岛仔能帮你 | | --- | --- | | 看今天的安排 | 月历与当日时间线，合并多个日历和正式邮件邀请，提前提醒会议 | | 记住每周的事 | 待办支持单次提醒、每周指定日期重复或每天重复；下一次到来时恢复为待办 | | 专心做一件事 | 专注与休息计时，收起时也能查看进度 | | 记得喝水 | 自定义每日目标、单次饮水量、提醒间隔与时段，记录错误可撤销 | 日历可接入 **飞书、钉钉、企业微信、iCloud、自定义 CalDAV 和兼容的 Exchange ActiveSync**，也能导入 `.ics` 文件。相同日程合并去重；支持全天、跨天和重复日程。 日程可按日期浏览，月历能看农历和节气。新建本机日程时可直接选日期和时间。在 **设置 → 通用** 可把公历、农历或两者一起放到岛上常驻。 本机新建或导入的日程保存在本机；远程日历为只读同步。程序退出、电脑关机或睡眠期间无法持续提醒。 ## 文件先放岛上，刚复制的字也能找回 ![文件置物架与剪贴板历史：拖入文件、重新复制文字、固定常用内容](docs/images/readme/shelf.webp) **文件置物架**：拖入文件临时收集，点击打开、定位原文件，或拖出到其他应用。移除记录不会删除原文件。 **文字剪贴板**：找回最近复制的 30 条文字，点一下重新复制，常用内容可以固定。历史保存在本机，重启后仍可查看；可在 **设置 → 待办与置物 → 剪贴板** 中关闭。密码管理器标记为敏感的内容不记录。 在置物架或剪贴板页点「保持展开」，鼠标移开后面板仍会留在桌面，方便连续拖放或复制。 ## 验证码少切一次窗口，邮件也能直接读 ![验证码大卡点击复制与邮件正文阅读](docs/images/readme/mail.webp) 连接多个邮箱，在岛上查看来信、识别验证码并点击复制。邮件支持正文阅读与独立全文窗口，网页链接交给默认浏览器打开；正式日历邀请可进入日程。支持已读／未读切换、全部已读、移到回收站及恢复；默认仅在本机整理，可在邮件设置中开启「同步邮件操作到邮箱」。 支持 **QQ、163、126、腾讯企业邮、iCloud、Gmail 和自定义 IMAP**。验证码可设置在 30／60／300 秒后自动隐藏，覆盖列表、正文与通知；主动查看后会再次隐藏。 - basic_info.description: Goal: an Xbox Series title (your own dump) on PC as the Series X version at 4K with ray tracing, picture matching the Xbox first (textures, lighting), then 30+ fps. Porting, not emulating. RX 7900 XTX first. No game files.

content.readme:
# VIctory on an RX 7900 XTX

A fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a compatibility layer
that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from files the user supplies.

## The goal

**The Series X version at 4K output (drawn at 1440p) with ray tracing on,
looking the way it does on the Xbox**, on an AMD RX 7900 XTX first.

In this order:

1. **A correct picture.** Textures and models reach full detail and stay there
   (no pop-in or pop-out, no flickering trees), and ray-traced lighting is right:
   not too dark, not too bright, no flicker.
2. **Then the frame rate:** 30 fps or more with ray tracing on, then as high a
   frame rate and as low frame times as the PC allows.
3. **Then smaller PCs:** 32 GB (later 16 GB) of RAM and smaller cards.

The way there is **porting, not emulating**: patching the title's renderer so it
behaves the way a PC renderer does, rather than having the layer watch and copy
the console's shared memory every frame. Shaders are translated ahead of time
into a versioned store that is kept between builds. The Series S profile and
ray tracing off stay available.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's developer
or publisher.

## Where it stands (2026-11-26)

Tested on one machine only: Windows 11, Intel i9-12900K, 64 GB RAM, Radeon
RX 7900 XTX, renderer patches 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 on. Runs of 270 s in a city
street: standing still, then walking and turning the camera.

| Version | Standing | Walking | RAM |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Series X, 4K drawn at 1440p, ray tracing on (the goal)** | 99 ms (10 fps) | ~110 ms (9 fps) | 45 GB |
| Series X, 4K drawn at 1440p, ray tracing off | 49 ms (20 fps) | ~62 ms (16 fps) | 45 GB |
| Series X, 1080p output, ray tracing off | 40 ms (25 fps) | ~43 ms (23 fps) | 42 GB |
| Series S, ray tracing off | 43 ms (23 fps) | ~64 ms (16 fps) | 37 GB |

Fixed 2026-11-26: trees and palms dropping out for a few frames, and most of the
lighting swinging between too dark and too bright in lamp-lit rooms. Both came from
indirect draws whose arguments sit in renderer patch 1's in-place memory being
prepared before the title's culling had written them; they are now prepared one at
a time right before they run (`VICTORY_PORT_CONSTANTS_ORDER`, on by default, about
2-5 ms). Rooms lit only by bounced light are no longer black with ray tracing
(`VICTORY_AMBIENT_RT=0.7,1.5`, which `Play-Watched.ps1 -RayTracing` sets).

Still open: models and textures stay at their lowest detail for a long time while
the title streams (worst in the intro): the title paces its streaming by its own
frames, so it loads about three times slower at 10 fps than at 30; ray-traced
structures of moving objects are partly corrupt (the rays follow some 450 stray
pointers a frame).

Earlier measurements with ray tracing off:

| | |
|---|---|
| City street, Series S profile, renderer patches 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 on | about 45 ms a frame (about 22 fps, 44.9 ms in run merge-5) |
| Same, patches 1, 2, 5 and 6 | 45.6 ms, p95 47 ms |
| Same, patches 1, 2 and 5 | 47.3 ms (about 21 fps), p95 49 ms |
| Series X profile, patches 1+2 | about 53 ms (about 19 fps) |
| Same scene before the patches | 57-75 ms (13-17 fps) |
| Shaders the title uses that translate | all of them (25,790 of 25,985; the rest are unused geometry shaders) |
| Memory | about 30 GB of private memory, 10.5 GB of VRAM: **64 GB of RAM recommended** for now |

It started at 280 ms a frame in the same scenes three days earlier. What sets
the frame now is the one thread that submits the title's work to the card
(about 40 ms); the card itself needs about 36 ms and now waits about 7 ms a frame with nothing queued.

### Renderer patches (off by default while they are tested)

| Switch | What it does |
|---|---|
| `VICTORY_PORT_CONSTANTS=1` | The title's 174 MB constants heap is read by the card where the title writes it: no uploads, no fills |
| `VICTORY_PORT_DESCRIPTORS=1` | The title's descriptor-table stores are patched (byte-checked) to report the slots they write, instead of a scan of ~600,000 slots a frame |
| `VICTORY_PORT_CBV=1` | Translated shaders read constant buffers in place as raw bytes (~22,000 fills a frame to none; -4.7 ms) |
| `VICTORY_PORT_GUARD=1` | The write guards' lock is shared by faults and refreshes, with a claim per 64 KiB block; the submission's planning runs beside it (title threads' waits 29 ms to ~2 ms a frame; -2 ms) |
| `VICTORY_PORT_JOURNAL=1` | The heaps' records are asked for at the title's submit, and the journal's notes are split into 64 parts with locks of their own (the submit thread's waits ~5 ms + 1 ms to ~0.3 ms; -1 to -3 ms) |

|---|---|
| `--console series-s` | The Series S profile: 1080p output, about 5 ms faster, a softer picture |

content.readme: # Xbox Emulator **Running the Xbox Series X|S library on PC. A continuation of [drycheetah84/TomBox](https://github.com/drycheetah84/TomBox).** The runtime reimplements the console's platform layer (Xbox-flavoured Direct3D 12, precompiled RDNA2 shaders, unified-memory textures, system libraries) so dumped, already-decrypted Xbox Series X|S builds run as normal Windows processes. It is not tied to any single title. This repo tracks our continuation — new titles brought up, platform calls extended, shader stages unlocked. Uses legally obtained, already-decrypted dumps. The runtime does no key extraction or package decryption. **Source code:** the emulator's Rust workspace is in this repo: [`crates/`](crates/), [`tools/`](tools/) and `Cargo.toml`. It contains no game files, binaries or build output. **Contributing:** pull requests are welcome, especially console library functions still marked missing in the [library map](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md). content.readme:
Airhand

High-performance, low-latency remote desktop
QUIC transport · hardware encoding and decoding · up to 120 fps
Windows · macOS · Linux · Android · iOS · browser

English · 简体中文

--- Airhand is a **high-performance, low-latency** remote desktop: the screen is encoded on the GPU (AV1 / HEVC / H.264) at up to 120 fps and sent over QUIC; when the network slows down it skips to the latest frame instead of letting lag pile up; and the mouse pointer is drawn locally, so it moves without delay. The same program is both the **host** (the device being controlled) and the **controller** (the device you control it from). The two sides meet through a **relay server** that you deploy yourself. It's small, and Docker Compose deploys it with one command. Enter the other side's 6-digit **control code** to connect. > [!NOTE] > **Work in progress (0.4.0).** Build the relay, clients and web service from the same v10 revision; earlier builds cannot be mixed. Video uses one QUIC stream per frame. [Protocol versions](docs/development.md#protocol-versions) ## Performance Every stage from capture to display is built for low latency: - **Hardware encoding and decoding**: the host encodes on the GPU (NVENC / Quick Sync / AMF, VideoToolbox, MediaCodec) in low-latency mode without B-frames; the controller decodes on the GPU (WebCodecs / MediaCodec). Measured with a 4K screen streamed at 1080p, hardware AV1 encoding takes about 7 ms per frame (RTX graphics card) - **The best format**: AV1 > HEVC > H.264, automatically picking the most efficient format both sides support; scaling and color conversion use SIMD, and all buffers are reused - **No lag build-up**: the host limits the bytes in flight (≈ bitrate × (RTT + 50 ms)) and skips to the latest frame on a slow network; the bitrate follows the measured queueing delay and bandwidth on every acknowledgement, backing off within a few hundred milliseconds and recovering gradually - **Direct path**: besides the relay, the two ends punch a direct path through their NATs (on the same LAN, or whenever the NAT isn't symmetric), so video and audio stop detouring through the server; the lower-latency path is picked automatically, and if the direct path breaks the session falls back to the relay without dropping - **QUIC + BBR**: BBR congestion control is steadier than Cubic on lossy networks such as Wi-Fi or long-distance links; control messages, audio and video are queued separately, so mouse input and pings never wait behind a large frame; the relay only forwards bytes and never parses the video - **Loss doesn't stall the picture**: each frame travels on its own QUIC stream, so a lost packet only holds up that frame. A frame that keeps not arriving is abandoned (no more retransmitting stale data) and the encoder continues from a long-term reference frame the controller already has (reference invalidation) instead of sending a large keyframe (Windows H.264, NVIDIA AV1; other encoders send a keyframe) - **Decode and show**: the decoder runs in low-latency mode, and each frame is drawn to a desynchronized canvas as soon as it's decoded, without waiting for vsync - **Local pointer**: the remote cursor's shape is mirrored locally, and moving it happens locally - **Low bandwidth**: no frames are sent while the screen is still, so an idle desktop uses almost nothing; sessions that aren't on screen drop to 5 fps See [How it works → Video](docs/architecture.md#video) for details. ## Features - **Windows system service**: the lock screen, the sign-in screen and UAC prompts can be seen and controlled, and the computer can be reached after boot, before anyone signs in - **Works with the monitor off** (Windows): when the host's monitor is switched off (or there's none), a virtual display fills in automatically; while a controller is connected the screen doesn't turn off and the computer doesn't sleep. On a Mac the same goes for a closed laptop lid (on a power adapter) or a Mac mini with no display - **Smooth on a Mac's Wi-Fi** (macOS): AirDrop's Wi-Fi peer-to-peer link (AWDL) keeps borrowing a Mac's wireless card, which makes remote control over Wi-Fi stutter now and then. The controller says so when it happens, and an option in the menu pauses AWDL while a remote session runs on Wi-Fi (as host or controller) and resumes it afterwards - **Privacy mode** (Windows, macOS): with one click the remote computer's monitors all go blank and its keyboard and mouse stop working, so only you can see and control it; it ends by itself after you disconnect, with the remote screen locked first - **Fixed control codes**: they survive restarts, upgrades and even server restarts until you change them yourself - **Console**: browser-style tabs to control several computers at once, plus a multi-screen overview to watch the

content.readme: **vork is a 3D and VFX engine built for AI agents.** Agents write the whole scene as code, including their own shaders, materials, cameras and physics, and vork renders it on the GPU. The core API fits in about 2,500 tokens. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03cfa020-be40-483a-89af-1ef77467b7a0 **One million birds, each on its own path.** 192 frames at 1080p rendered in 97 seconds on a single NVIDIA L4. Blender EEVEE at the same sample count is projected at 13–18 minutes. [How we measured](#million-birds-measured-movies-projected-blender-times) · [how it's made](examples/murmuration/) · [credits](examples/murmuration/CREDITS) - **Built for agents:** a small API that agents can extend with their own GPU programs. - **Fast:** 1.1–2.3× faster than EEVEE on default stills and movies, and about 8–11× on the bird flock. [Speed, with the qualifications](#speed-with-the-qualifications). - **Native GPU engine:** written in Rust and Slang, runs on Vulkan and Metal (Linux, Windows, macOS). - **No GPU needed:** render on Voyager's cloud GPUs with [vork cloud](https://voyager.so/vork/cloud). ## Paste this to your agent [Install vork](#install), then paste: > Run `vork init my-shot`, read `vork help`, render a preview and inspect the image. > Refine the camera and lighting before rendering at final quality. Read the > relevant help topic when you need a feature the first page doesn't explain. vork is written in Rust and Slang, with GPU rendering through Vulkan and Metal. An agent writes a scene, renders it, looks at the result and revises the code. There is no editor to drive. Most creative tools expose controls that a person can operate. An agent can also write a shader in the middle of a shot. vork gives it geometry, ray queries and GPU execution, then lets scene programs define materials, cameras, light propagation, simulation and compositing. Ordinary shots need only scene data; the programming hooks are there when the shot needs something unusual. Source-available and free during the research preview. ## Start here After [installing vork](#install), create a working project: ```sh vork init my-shot && cd my-shot vork skills add vork render scene.json --out render.png ``` Open `render.png`, change a colour or camera position in `scene.json`, and render again. The starter uses only bundled sphere, box and grid primitives: no downloads, no GPU needed to initialize. Use `vork init my-shot --language typescript` or `--language python` for editable `scene.ts` or `scene.py` alongside the ready-to-render JSON. The generated README explains regeneration and SDK requirements. Existing files are never overwritten. The default `std/final` profile is warmed by setup; use `--profile std/draft` for quicker previews. ## What you can make The examples include code, preparation commands and credits. Large downloaded assets and footage stay outside Git; the recipes fetch them or accept a local path. The images here are stills from these shots. content.readme:
WinRust

Your Windows, minus the bloat.
The taskbar, File Explorer, file search and Task Manager rebuilt in Rust: native, tiny and fast.

⬇ Download WinRust.exe · Install · What's inside · Community

English | Русский | 日本語 | Português (Brasil) | 简体中文

![The WinRust bar with its settings menu, Ruby theme](docs/screenshots/taskbar.webp) > **Read this first.** WinRust turns off Windows Search, hides the taskbar and can turn off Explorer as the shell. The exe is not code-signed, so SmartScreen will warn you. A restore point is created before install, but try it on a spare machine or a VM first. ## Why WinRust - **Fast.** A folder window opens in 60 ms instead of 420 ms, a search over the whole C: drive takes 45 ms ([measurements](#benchmark)). - **Light.** The whole shell takes 46 MB of memory, explorer.exe took 366 MB. - **Native.** Small Win32 programs: no .NET, no Electron. - **Reversible.** Every value is saved before it is changed and put back on uninstall. One button removes everything. - **Yours.** Eight styles (Ruby, Terminal, Floating dock, Windows 98 and more), any colour, the bar on any edge, English, Русский, 日本語 or Português. ## See it | Run (Win+R) | File manager | |---|---| | ![Run box with recent commands](docs/screenshots/run.webp) | ![rust-explorer, Ruby theme](docs/screenshots/explorer.webp) | **Task Manager** (Russian UI) ![Task Manager](docs/screenshots/task-manager.webp) ## Install 1. Download `WinRust.exe` from the [latest release](https://github.com/Lemxy/WinRust/releases/latest) (Windows 10/11, x64). 2. Run it as administrator. 3. Pick **Express (recommended)** and press **Install**: search, Task Manager, the bar, Settings, disk analysis and the photo viewer, nothing removed and Explorer left in place. Or pick **Custom (advanced)** to tick the components yourself, including `rust-explorer` (replaces the Windows Explorer shell; also the **Replace Explorer** switch behind the gear on the topbar row) and the extras. They are installed in the right order; one that fails or is skipped does not stop the others, and the last page lists each component with its result. Windows Search is optional: on a stripped Windows (for example a debloated LTSC image without the Windows Search service) that step is skipped with a warning instead of failing the install. If UAC asks for **another administrator's** password, the per-user settings (startup entries, scheduled tasks, PowerShell profile, search permissions) still go to the user who is signed in, not to the administrator you typed. If the installer cannot tell who that is, it stops before changing anything. **Automatic updates:** after the first install, a `WinRust-update` scheduled task (runs as SYSTEM, no UAC prompt) checks the latest release at boot and once a day. It downloads the new `WinRust.exe` (and any program a release ships on its own), checks each file against a manifest signed with the project's key (a tampered or unsigned release is refused); the new `WinRust.exe` then replaces the installed programs that differ from the ones it carries. Only files that are already installed are replaced. A running program switches to the new version the next time it starts (sign-in or reboot). Log: `%ProgramData%\plugin-launcher\install.log` (`autoupdate:` lines). To turn it off, disable the `WinRust-update` task in Task Scheduler; **Remove WinRust** deletes it. **Manual update:** download the new `WinRust.exe` from the releases page, run it as administrator and press **Update** on the Express card (it reinstalls what is installed and adds what is missing), or use Custom. An existing `rust-explorer` stays ticked. Your settings and the saved original Windows values stay. The installer is in English. Its corner holds a language drop-down — English, Русский, 日本語, Português (Brasil), 简体中文; the same list sits behind the gear on the bar (**Bar settings → Language**), and rust-settings has it on its Personalization page (**Interface language**). The choice is stored in `%ProgramData%\WinRust\lang.txt` (`en`, `ru`, `ja`, `pt`, `zh`); the program you switch in repaints at once, the other programs read it when they start, so restart them (or sign out) after a change. ## Remove - **Remove WinRust** on the installer's first page undoes everything: Windows Search, the taskbar, Explorer and the services come back. - Without the installer (for example, antivirus deleted it): **Settings → Apps → Installed apps → WinRust → Uninstall** does the same as Remove WinRust. - One plugin at a time: `plugin-launcher un
